title: Free walking speed in a straight corridor
criterion: travel time between 26 s and 34 s at 1.33 m/s (40 m corridor)
detail: All replicas inside the source band.

title: Movement around a corner
source: RiMEA 4.1.1, Annex 2, Test 6 (geometry adapted, see test_cases.md)
criterion: all 20 people round the corner and exit; no position inside a wall
detail: All 20 rounded the corner and left; no wall crossing in any frame.

title: Pre-movement (reaction) time distribution
criterion: each person starts at their assigned uniform(10, 100) s time (observed first movement within 2.5 s of the assigned delay)
detail: Every observed start matches its assigned reaction time.

title: Bottleneck effect between two rooms
source: RiMEA 4.1.1, Annex 2, Test 12 (behaviour documented, not an exclusion criterion in the source)
criterion: congestion forms in room 1 only: peak occupancy density room 1 > room 2 and room 2 stays below 1.5 people/m^2
detail: Queue forms before the corridor; room 2 stays free-flowing.

title: Exit assignment and route choice
source: RiMEA 4.1.1, Annex 2, Test 11 (200 people instead of 1,000; geometry adapted, see test_cases.md)
criterion: nearer exit preferred (majority) and alternative also used (>= 5%)
detail: Both exits used; the nearer one carries the majority, as expected.

title: Fundamental diagram vs Weidmann (1993)
source: Weidmann (1993), Kladek form as quoted in secondary literature (see test_cases.md); tolerance is a project choice
criterion: low-density speed within 20% of the curve, speed decreasing with density, RMSE <= 0.30 m/s (project tolerance)
detail: FAIL, reported as-is. Binned means [1.13, 1.21, 1.02, 1.01, 0.46, 0.34] m/s at densities [0.25, 0.75, 1.25, 1.75, 2.5, 4.5] people/m^2: the overall drop with density and the RMSE (0.188 m/s, inside the 0.30 tolerance) follow Weidmann, but the two lowest bins are not monotonic (sparse-corridor samples include queue-tail deceleration) and the highest bin stays faster than the empirical curve. Known model limitation, already noted in PROGRESS.md during P02: at crush densities the simulated flow runs above handbook values with the Helbing parameters. The monotonicity criterion was fixed before running and is not relaxed to hide this.
